extracted.intended_audience: PCI recommenders (associate-editor–style evaluators) handling preprints for Peer Community In (PCI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for PCI recommenders who manage evaluation of preprints: how to accept/reject, recruit reviewers, write recommendation texts, and perform editorial duties for Peer Community In.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance: scientific, methodological and ethical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI only accepts and recommends preprints of high scientific quality that are methodologically and ethically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A scientifically sound article should be accepted. A scientifically unsound one should not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender willingness and positive motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: You handle a manuscript evaluation only if you’re willing to: don’t feel obligated to take charge of an evaluation. You have to be positively motivated to do so because you are interested in the preprint (because of its background, the scientific question addressed, the methodology, the results, or the discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not agree to handle the evaluation of a preprint if you have not taken the time to read it, if you are not familiar with the subject, if you have no time to handle it in a timely manner, or if you’re not interested in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Editor in Chief, so you’re the only person responsible for the editorial decisions. If you have co-recommenders, you share this responsibility with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees do not make decisions; this is your duty. Your editorial decision should synthesize the most relevant comments of the reviews as well as your own points of criticism. State whether you disagree with some points raised by the reviewers. Feel free to reject an article at any step of the evaluation process if there are scientifically sound reasons justifying this rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of evaluation dependent on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation process (including reviews, your decisions, and author responses) is published by PCI only if you decide, at the end of the evaluation process, to accept the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation text requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you accept the article, you must write a recommendation text. This text describes the qualities of the preprint, including the subjective reasons for your interest in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation text is a short article (300–1500 words) with its own title, describes the context, explains why you find it interesting and why you decided to recommend it, and it is citable. This text also contains references (at a minimum the reference to the article being recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: No acceptance rate or quality notation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no acceptance rate to be reached. There is no quality notation among PCIs. No stars, no impact factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You only have to be interested in the article to handle its evaluation, and then sound articles are accepted, and unsound ones are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest prohibition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should not be in conflict of interest with the authors or with the content of the article. If you are, you must decline the invitation. You should not invite reviewers who are in conflict of interest with the authors or with the content of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PCI Code of Conduct; tone and constructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: General advice: Follow the PCI Code of conduct. Be kind, respectful and constructive in your decisions. Be open to new approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unconstructive, ambiguous, and unsupported comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer diversity when inviting referees
rubrics_metrics.description: When inviting referees for a preprint, keep in mind that a large gender, career stage and geographic diversity is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to keep to the deadlines at each steps in the process, it shows respect towards the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly reply to the invitation on the website by accepting or declining. Invite reviewers as soon as you agree to handle the manuscript. Send invitations to 5–10 potential reviewers within 48 hours, and then send reminders and/or new invitations until you find at least two reviewers willing to review the preprint. This process should ideally take no more than a week. Post your editorial decision or write your recommendation text within 10 days after receiving the reviews or the revised version of the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to personalize your invitation letters as much as possible in order to maximize responsivity of invited reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing sufficient quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible for ensuring at least two good quality reviews before making decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send reminders to reviewers who have agreed to evaluate the article until you get at least two good quality reviews (see PCI reviewer guide).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and technical checks not required
rubrics_metrics.description: No need to examine whether the article falls within the scope of the PCI. No need to check the format of the references. No need to check for plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism checks are handled by the managing board. Do not spend recommender time on these checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, typographical and language quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to typographical and other errors. A recommended article must be as close to perfect as possible in terms of its form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the language is poor, mention it to the authors and suggest that they check for typos and/or have it proofread by a native English speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, code and materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that data, scripts, simulation code, software parameters, etc. are available to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for repository link/DOI or appendix providing access to data and code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting delays and suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform the managing board if you are delayed or if you are unexpectedly unable to carry out your recommender duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the managing board if you suspect scientific misconduct.
